Chapter Five: Designing Environments and Routines for Success
Have you ever noticed how your surroundings can nudge you toward certain choices—almost without you realizing it? The spaces we move through, and the routines that fill our days, quietly shape what we do, again and again.
Think of environment design as your secret weapon for building better habits. It's all about making the good stuff easier—and putting a few speed bumps in the way of things you'd rather avoid. Imagine it like a gardener setting up the perfect spot for each plant to thrive.
Even small tweaks in your environment can lead to big changes in what you actually do. Picture this: you put a bowl of fresh fruit right on your kitchen counter. Suddenly, grabbing a healthy snack becomes almost automatic. On the flip side, if you stash the cookies out of sight, you’ll find you’re much less tempted. The trick is to make the cues for your positive habits pop out, while keeping the triggers for your not-so-great ones hidden away.
But it’s not just your physical space that matters. The people around you, and the routines you follow, play a huge role too. We tend to pick up on the habits of those we spend time with, often without even noticing. So, if you join a running club, for example, you’ll probably find yourself lacing up your shoes for a jog more often—just because that’s what everyone else is doing.
Want some practical ways to design your environment for success? Here are a few ideas:
First, try restructuring your spaces. Set up your home, your office, or even your digital world so that the habits you want are right at your fingertips. Like keeping a book on your nightstand if you want to read before bed.
Next, add a little friction to your bad habits. Make them just a bit harder to do. For instance, you could delete distracting apps from your phone or move them somewhere less convenient. Out of sight, out of mind, right?
And don’t forget the power of social influence. Spend more time with people who already have the habits you want to build. It’s amazing how their energy and actions can rub off on you.
Now, let’s talk about routines. Routines are like the backbone of your day, and if you anchor a new habit to something you already do, it’s so much easier to remember and stick with it. That’s what habit stacking is all about—using an existing routine as a launchpad for a new behavior.
The real magic here? It’s not about relying on willpower. When you shape your environment and routines just right, the path to your new habit becomes the path of least resistance. Suddenly, change doesn’t feel like a struggle—it feels natural.
So, when you thoughtfully shape your surroundings and daily rhythms, you give your good habits a place to flourish, while the bad ones fade away. That’s how you turn change from something you wrestle with, into something that just fits seamlessly into your life.
